Question: Consider the reinforced process \((X_n,\mu_n)\) on a finite state space \(S\), where \(\mu_n\in\mathcal P(S)\) evolves by \(\mu_{n+1}=(1-\gamma_{n+1})\mu_n+\gamma_{n+1}\delta_{X_{n+1}}\), and \(X_{n+1}\) is sampled from the resurrected kernel \(K_{\mu_n}(X_n,\cdot)\) with \(K_\mu(x,y)=P(x,y)+q(x)\mu(y)\) and \(q(x)=1-\sum_{z\in S}P(x,z)\) for a sub-Markov kernel \(P\) on \(S\). Let \(\nu_1,\ldots,\nu_\kappa\) denote the quasi-stationary distributions of the associated killed chain, indexed so that \(\nu_\kappa\) is the one associated with the largest Perron value, and let \(W_n\) be the reinforcement-weight sequence. Assume that the cemetery state \(\partial\) is accessible from every state in \(S\), the Perron values \(\rho_\alpha\) are pairwise distinct, the initial condition satisfies \(S=\overline{\operatorname{supp}(\mu_0)}\) almost surely and \(X_0\in \operatorname{supp}(\mu_0)\), and the step-size sequence \((\gamma_n)_{n\ge 1}\subset(0,1)\) is eventually non-increasing with \(\sum_{n\ge 1}\gamma_n=\infty\) and \(\gamma_n\log n\to 0\). Which description gives the complete classification of the almost sure limiting behavior of \((\mu_n)\) according to the regime of \(\sum_{n\ge 0} 1/W_n\)?
Predicted label: 'B'
Predicted text: 'If \\(\\sum_{n\\ge 0} 1/W_n=\\infty\\), then \\(\\mu_n\\) converges almost surely to \\(\\nu_\\kappa\\), the quasi-stationary distribution associated with the largest Perron value. If \\(\\sum_{n\\ge 0} 1/W_n<\\infty\\), then \\(\\mu_n\\) converges almost surely to one of the quasi-stationary distributions \\(\\nu_1,\\ldots,\\nu_\\kappa\\), and \\(\\mathbb P(\\lim_{n\\to\\infty}\\mu_n=\\nu_\\kappa)>0\\); however, for every \\(\\alpha<\\kappa\\), the event that \\(X_n\\in\\overline{S_\\alpha}\\) for all sufficiently large \\(n\\) and \\(\\mu_n\\to\\nu_\\alpha\\) has probability \\(0\\).'
Correct label: 'A'
Correct text: 'If \\(\\sum_{n\\ge 0} 1/W_n=\\infty\\), then \\(\\mu_n\\) converges almost surely to \\(\\nu_\\kappa\\), the quasi-stationary distribution associated with the largest Perron value. If \\(\\sum_{n\\ge 0} 1/W_n<\\infty\\), then \\(\\mu_n\\) converges almost surely to one of the quasi-stationary distributions \\(\\nu_1,\\ldots,\\nu_\\kappa\\); moreover \\(\\mathbb P(\\lim_{n\\to\\infty}\\mu_n=\\nu_\\kappa)>0\\), and in fact for every \\(\\alpha\\in\\{1,\\ldots,\\kappa\\}\\), the event that \\(X_n\\in\\overline{S_\\alpha}\\) for all sufficiently large \\(n\\) (where \\(\\overline{S_\\alpha}\\) denotes the closed component associated with \\(\\nu_\\alpha\\)) and \\(\\mu_n\\to\\nu_\\alpha\\) has positive probability.'
Exact Match: 0.0
